_comment: A/B TEST FILE - DIRECTION NOT VERIFIED. Do not treat as part of the realism stack until tested. The trap 'reaction' tables for a BOUNCING ball (trap.reactionTrapBall.reactionBoundBall.*) are all proven READ by the exe (fn 0x14405f170 interpolates reactionTime between paraMin and paraMax by incoming ball speed, then blends in two per-player factors, so it is attribute-dependent). What is NOT established is the SENSE of reactionTime: a delay before the player can act (larger = harder) or an anticipation window (larger = easier). The stock values fit either reading. This file LENGTHENS the bouncing-ball times 0.40 -> 0.50/0.55. Test it for one match: if players look clumsier receiving bobbling balls, the delay reading is right and this belongs in the stack; if they look sharper, invert it (try 0.30/0.25). NOTE the receiver is probably ALREADY penalised by a bobbling ball without this file: the proven first-touch error function 0x144079a70 has a ball-height branch (compare against 0.163 m) that appears to raise the base touch error 5 -> 10 deg and its multiplier 10 -> 15 for a ball off the ground; stock hops (~5 cm) sit right at that threshold, the bobble-pitch.json hops (~14 cm) clear it. That reading of the 0.163 compare is very likely but not traced to certainty. Apply: python tools/gameplay_tune.py apply tools/data/tunings/bobble-receive-AB.json --stack
